circuit_role: Fix the target and all universal quantifiers.
publisher_statement_or_check: HC_m over every field, and PERM_m outside characteristic two, require size greater than m^(c(log₂ m)^(1/3)).
review_finding: M.1 transfers the same circuit to a comparison field of its characteristic. In a flat field E.11 excludes the circuit. In a contracting field K.3 and K.6 assert and deny the same accelerator. The branch rates give the universal coefficient 1/1600² after a characteristic-dependent cutoff.
independent_evidence_scope: 14A–C reconstruct the flat derivation, concrete tree and weighted compiler. 14E follows the interfaces, scale match, nonzero-field contradiction and final rate comparison. Global build and Comparator carry their own receipts.
remaining_obligation: Complete separate human reconstructions of the geometry beneath D.2, F.2–F.5, I.1–I.2 and machine implementations J.3–J.4 and K.4–K.6 for an independently derived proof throughout.
review_detail: HC sums one-cycle permutations and PERM sums all permutations of an m-by-m matrix. The review concerns exact computation.

circuit_role: Define which candidate circuits every branch must cover.
publisher_statement_or_check: Size counts a straight-line list of variables, field constants, sums and products, with earlier gates reusable.
review_finding: E.4 collects one cofactor per original gate for each cut. K.2 collects coefficient contributions in a ring on ordered predecessor sockets, guesses nonuniform coefficient names and sums weighted accepting runs.
independent_evidence_scope: 13A gate-index induction and 14C forest invariant. Four circuits over four rings gave 3,640 comparisons with gate evaluation, including cancellation and repeated references.
remaining_obligation: A bit-cost or uniform-advice circuit model requires its own representation and lookup bounds.
review_detail: Each circuit may depend on m. Evaluation on all points of a finite field would be weaker than equality of formal polynomials.

circuit_role: Convert wire exponents and cut decompositions into spectral upper bounds.
publisher_statement_or_check: A spectral point values a binary wire by 2 to its distance exponent; the hub construction routes cut terms through auxiliaries.
review_finding: Equality wires copy each logical end index to its hub, and one shared middle index selects the product. Co-located tables multiply while their distinct logical legs remain separate.
independent_evidence_scope: 12D reconstructed the local maps and boundary cases and exactly tested 116 placements and 600 output entries. E.10's restrictions on end operations are checked at a distinct logical-party caller. 12E rebuilt Paper.Prices and queried A.3 directly.
remaining_obligation: For applications with additional restrictions on operations at end parties, verify those hypotheses before merging physical labels. Audit A.2's restriction framework beyond the hub construction if relied on elsewhere.
review_detail: An ordinary restriction can have a nonidentity map at a site where an end and a hub coincide. E.10 retains separate logical labels when pulling back the geometric witness.

circuit_role: Select one spectral point that retains all required comparisons.
publisher_statement_or_check: A spectral point below a gauge keeps every triple that the gauge keeps for every multiplier.
review_finding: Zorn minimality, the radius and localization give exact multiplicativity for the same witness; zero factors need a separate case.
independent_evidence_scope: Independent reconstruction; pass-10 build and pass-11B theorem readback; two weakening counterexamples.
remaining_obligation: Any use requiring effective or unique selection would need a further theorem. A.5 supplies existence.
review_detail: An arbitrary infimum can fail submultiplicativity. Testing a triple only at the unit can miss a violating multiplier.

circuit_role: Produce asymptotic tensor covers behind the contracting laws.
publisher_statement_or_check: Comparison at every spectral point implies covers of high powers by at most 2^(εN) products of N factors.
review_finding: If the replacement-cost infimum excludes strict exchange, A.5 gives a contradicting single spectral point. Strict exchange recursively eliminates copies down to bounded residual cost.
independent_evidence_scope: 13B derived the weighted leaf count and common-power use in G.2; the full module is in the combined build.
remaining_obligation: Reconstruct A.5's separation mechanism at full generality, including all hypotheses in the upper functional.
review_detail: This is a bridge to section G. Existence of a spectral point alone provides no quantitative cover.

circuit_role: Extend a spectral witness for the price and flat-branch constructions.
publisher_statement_or_check: One extended spectral point respects the geometric-mean bound on every tensor and is exact on one designated old tensor.
review_finding: The intermediate gauge agrees on every old tensor. Localization and A.5 force equality at the designated tensor of the selected point.
independent_evidence_scope: Passes 10 and 11B reconstructed the selection; pass 10 rebuilt the complete target module and queried the theorem.
remaining_obligation: E.8 now identifies the positive product of old pair wires and the old selector; any different application must identify its own simultaneous observables.
review_detail: For zero spectral value, nonnegativity and domination suffice. A single preserved value need not determine the entire old point.

circuit_role: Add all fan and midpoint labels to one price.
publisher_statement_or_check: One extended price keeps every old distance and upper-bounds every pair by the expectation under a joint random map.
review_finding: Preserving the product of all old wires and coordinatewise domination forces equality for each old wire. Common compact limits retain all inequalities.
independent_evidence_scope: Independent source reconstruction, finite controls, and complete Paper.Prices replay in pass 10.
remaining_obligation: A use with infinite-valued label maps would require additional hypotheses beyond the stated measurable finite-image setting.
review_detail: The two coordinates in one expectation use the same random outcome. New distances may lie strictly below the expectation.

circuit_role: Bound the number of states in the two-wire decomposition.
publisher_statement_or_check: One positive κ upper-bounds log P(E) by κ√E for every E and gives the matching asymptotic lower rate.
review_finding: Interleaving fixed-energy symbols proves that the supremum of log P(E)/√E is the full limit. The same supremum bounds every index. Frobenius coordinates and the partition product give κ=π/√3 for natural logs.
independent_evidence_scope: 11A examined the consumer. 12D reconstructed B.1, checked finite interleavings and partition counts, and rebuilt the ten-module Paper.Identity closure including B.1.
remaining_obligation: The review's explicit normalization is independently derived and has finite controls. A separate Lean statement of that value remains open. B.3 uses existence and commonality of κ.
review_detail: A lower asymptotic evaluated at a potentially zero coefficient index would be invalid. The reconstruction tracks the two uses separately.

circuit_role: Provide one integral family for both cut routings.
publisher_statement_or_check: The crossing identity decomposes two matching wires into coefficient tensors with complementary cut complexities.
review_finding: One signed minor expansion factors the coefficient across AD|BC; reflection gives the complementary-degree expansion across AB|CD for the same tensor. The surviving equal-rank sign has even parity in the printed convention.
independent_evidence_scope: 11A verified a finite coefficient family and field cancellation. 12D derived truncation, signs and reflection, checked four signed polynomial determinants and rebuilt all ten publisher modules for Paper.Identity.
remaining_obligation: A separate formal statement of the review's explicit printed-order minor sign remains open. The publisher's integral B.2 and its complementary-degree decomposition have been replayed.
review_detail: This is a tensor identity. The later numbered inequality (B.2) is a separate statement.

circuit_role: Obtain two compatible bounds for one price table.
publisher_statement_or_check: There exist joint nonnegative hub weights in a squared budget that bound both routings.
review_finding: Selecting one large spectral summand supplies the same index for degree and complementary degree. Uniform counting errors and compactness preserve one feasible pair.
independent_evidence_scope: Reconstructed and stress-tested in 11A; Paper.Crossing compiled in pass 9. 12D's companion note reconstructs A.3 routing and tests repeated labels.
remaining_obligation: Any stronger inference that restricts which physical sites can apply nonidentity maps must check the caller's hypothesis separately. The joint two-cut price inequality uses ordinary restriction monotonicity.
review_detail: Separate maximizers can violate the joint budget. The transfer to a general price approximates all eight labels at once. Pass 12D supplied the common normalization and two degree bounds used here.

circuit_role: Pass the crossing bound into C.2 in a scalar form.
publisher_statement_or_check: Adding the joint inequalities and applying two quadratic estimates eliminates both auxiliary weights.
review_finding: The derivation works pointwise with variable local wire distances as weights before translation averaging.
independent_evidence_scope: 11A independent algebra and eight-point metric counterexample; formal implication compiled in pass 9.
remaining_obligation: Maintain the simultaneous squared budget and a fixed positive Young parameter whenever taking the mean.
review_detail: A bound optimized separately for each cut would not imply this scalar display.

circuit_role: Turn two-dimensional price averages into a parallelogram law.
publisher_statement_or_check: The homogenized mean seminorm obeys the parallelogram equality.
review_finding: The numbered crossing display passes to the root-mean-square length and then to its homogeneous limit. The upper parallelogram inequality alone suffices at C.1's endpoint.
independent_evidence_scope: Source reconstruction, pass-9 full dependency replay with direct axiom readback, and 11A caller audit.
remaining_obligation: For an independent derivation of the complete mean argument, audit the remaining translation-invariant mean and seminorm steps in full generality. The preceding counting, determinant and routing arguments have now been reconstructed.
review_detail: The bound on fixed displacements controls all mean terms. Individual fans need not converge ordinarily.

circuit_role: Establish the midpoint curvature inequality used by the geometry.
publisher_statement_or_check: A midpoint m on an endpoint pair at distance 2D satisfies the CN inequality for every test point z.
review_finding: First A→∞ at fixed T removes the intercept; then the error is at most (6D²+6Db+b²)/T for b=d(z,m).
independent_evidence_scope: Independent endpoint derivation, exact boundary checks, and a fresh 44-module replay of Paper.Fan in pass 9.
remaining_obligation: Preserve the midpoint hypotheses and the order of limiting arguments in downstream interpretations.
review_detail: The coefficient is uniform in T for fixed points. The intermediate seminorm may depend on T.

circuit_role: Realize every price inside one complete CAT(0) price space.
publisher_statement_or_check: Adding compatible midpoints, identifying zero distances and completing realizes the old table as a metric pullback.
review_finding: The Cauchy estimate supplies one limiting midpoint for all test points and the compact price conditions persist on finite tables.
independent_evidence_scope: Pass 8 derived the completion and replayed two lemmas. In 12E the full Paper.Curvature module compiled as part of the fresh, pinned 54-module D.2 build, with fresh theorem and axiom readbacks.
remaining_obligation: At the mathematical level, finish the independent audit of how every finite configuration of the completion obtains its price and compare the source representation to the manuscript.
review_detail: The method allows distinct original labels to map to one point.

circuit_role: Supply quadrangle, rectangle and projection facts to the field split and flat argument.
publisher_statement_or_check: The CAT(0) toolkit deduces geometric estimates from CN, including equality constraints for flat quadrangles.
review_finding: Passes 7–8 located the exact equality and realization facts that D.2 needs.
independent_evidence_scope: Some toolkit uses received mathematical review in pass 7. Paper.Toolkit was freshly compiled within D.2's 54-module build. The individual toolkit declarations received no new direct readback.
remaining_obligation: Reconstruct the quadrangle, reflection and cube-filling cases relied upon by D.2, including their representation hypotheses.
review_detail: A weak diagonal-sum bound alone does not recover the equality structure used in the field alternative.

circuit_role: Ensure at least one branch applies to each field.
publisher_statement_or_check: For a field K either its prices satisfy the contracting condition or every finite Euclidean distance table is a K-price.
review_finding: Failure of contraction produces an extremal price; equality on transversal quadrangles and a cube construction give one table per configuration.
independent_evidence_scope: Pass 7 reconstructed eight steps conditionally and tested metric shortcuts. Pass 12E freshly rebuilt all 54 original project modules needed for D.2 and read back its actual type, rank-price bridge, Euclidean-configuration result and axioms.
remaining_obligation: Independently reconstruct the exchange, rigidity and cube-filling arguments at full generality. Pass 14E follows both alternatives to the same transferred circuit.
review_detail: Exhaustion is sufficient; disjointness of the two conditions is unnecessary.

circuit_role: Provide the permanent target for the branch grid reductions outside characteristic two.
publisher_statement_or_check: A grid bit sum with weights over a commutative ring admitting one half is a permanent of a matrix of size S ≥ 3|I| with the specified entries.
review_finding: Each local row pair gives coefficient 2h. With 2h=1 the squarefree coefficient counts exactly the grid weight with shared bits and padding. The same nonempty matrix degenerates in characteristic two.
independent_evidence_scope: 13C symbolic derivation, 512 formal coefficients over six finite layouts, signed enumeration, and a fresh Paper.Grids build.
remaining_obligation: The κ=3 grid projection is used in both audited branches when 2≠0. Any claim for permanent in characteristic two requires a new projection or a different argument.
review_detail: The affine substitution cost is a separate gate-count allowance. Characteristic two is outside this permanent argument.

circuit_role: Connect the target circuit to the flat branch's auxiliary polynomial.
publisher_statement_or_check: A permanent circuit at sufficient size parameter gives one for the network polynomial through affine substitution.
review_finding: For k≥2 and ℓ≥1 there are k(k−1)ℓ·2^((k−1)ℓ) incidences. The 3-per-incidence order fits E.3's uniform threshold. The affine substitution increases size by at most a factor of five.
independent_evidence_scope: 13C traced literals through E.1–E.3 and the five-gate encoding. Paper.Flat, including its E.3 declaration, was freshly compiled in the joint build.
remaining_obligation: E.11 consumes the grid size through integer bracketing. Extension to a different input family requires a grid embedding with its own dimension factor.
review_detail: M.2 supplies the all-characteristic HC route. The target matrix size and the gate cost of substituting an affine entry are distinct parameters.

circuit_role: Bring an arbitrary circuit, with gate reuse and cancellations, into the flat argument.
publisher_statement_or_check: The block-multilinear component is a sum over balanced subsets with at most L simple products per subset for an L-gate circuit.
review_finding: Strong induction on gate index groups the ordered contributions by original gate and balanced subset. Each key has one cofactor on the complementary variables, even for repeated operands.
independent_evidence_scope: 13A proof reconstruction, 441,920 finite coefficients, two-module induction, isolated E.4 readback, and a fresh full Paper.Flat build.
remaining_obligation: The cut sum and numerical caller are reconstructed in 14A. The stronger interpretation of a fixed paying cut independent of the spectral point would require additional information.
review_detail: Bounding rank across one shared flattening would exclude valid decompositions. The generic A.3 restriction is reconstructed in the 12D routing note. The mixed-cut circuit caller retains distinct logical end and hub labels.

circuit_role: Pay for combining the differently cut terms.
publisher_statement_or_check: For J permitted summands, the spectral value is bounded by J to the old-party exponent times the largest summand value.
review_finding: For fixed k and one spectral point, sort J^n cut words by multiplicities. A diagonal shared selector permits simultaneous permutations on the active ends. There are at most (n+1)^J types. Taking nth roots removes that factor, yielding Φ(t)≤J^g(P) max_A Φ(T_A).
independent_evidence_scope: 14A reconstructs the n→∞ limit at fixed alphabet, zero-base case, D=0 at this caller, and flattening-rank counterexamples for omitted support and interchanged max/min. 84 signed entries checked.
remaining_obligation: The conclusion allows the paying cut to depend on the common spectral point. General border maps retain the extraction-degree factor in the finite-power estimate.
review_detail: The common tensor is priced by one spectral point. Different words of the same multiplicity share one permutation label at every nontrivial output.

circuit_role: Control the exponent of a midpoint configuration for a fixed base spectral point.
publisher_statement_or_check: A sufficiently accurate scaled Euclidean approximation gives approximate midpoint convexity of the party exponent.
review_finding: Preserve the product of all old pair wires and the selector at the old midpoint map. Product saturation fixes every nonnegative loss. C.1 bounds moving q selector legs by q√(d(2R+4)). Choose d before any admissible witness and all triples on the finite configuration.
independent_evidence_scope: 14A derives d=min(1,η²/((q²+1)(2R+4))) and identifies the positive observable retained by A.7. Extension witnesses may differ across triples while inequalities concern the same old Φ.
remaining_obligation: The CAT(0) midpoint comparison and A.7 are upstream dependencies. The tolerance controls only the fixed finite label configuration and chosen error.
review_detail: Auxiliary extensions may vary by map while estimates return to the same base point.

circuit_role: Find a single spectral witness for the competing flat cuts.
publisher_statement_or_check: In the flat case a spectral point and scale approximate all distances of the finite configuration and bound its facet-centre exponent.
review_finding: Add all ternary half-cube positions before choosing Φ. Average the mapped facet centres over signs. Base loss Δ/2 and k midpoint losses Δ/(2k) give c g(P)≤√k+Δ in the one chosen witness.
independent_evidence_scope: 14A reconstructs simultaneous approximation on V′, endpoint collisions and the sign expectation. The 12C cube and varying-loss controls remain separate evidence.
remaining_obligation: At E.10, both hubs of every balanced cut must already be included in the finite configuration before the witness is chosen.
review_detail: The flat hypothesis supplies Euclidean approximation; A.5 alone does not select a Euclidean witness.

circuit_role: Lower-bound every circuit for the flat auxiliary polynomial.
publisher_statement_or_check: For k≥2 and ℓ≥100√k the stated bound gives log₂ L at least ℓk^(3/2)/16.
review_finding: The same Φ prices all original wires, candidate hub pairs and the end selector. For each maximizing cut, ℓS₁≤kG+ℓS₂+S₃log₂L; the two wire-error budgets sum to 3ℓNΔ. The publisher proves denominator 14 and states 16. The review derives strict denominator 12.
independent_evidence_scope: 14A checks 1,428 balanced hub directions. The independent scalar Lean receipt verifies 12b−a=1073/135000>0 as part of the implication; the circuit-level instantiation has its own replay evidence.
remaining_obligation: The stronger /12 is conditional on flatness and the original circuit-to-price hypotheses. Any stronger margin needs an improved estimate or structure beyond the exhibited /11 scalar obstruction.
review_detail: The size-preserving bridge for the printed variables matters when the lower bound is applied to the actual polynomial.

circuit_role: Translate the flat auxiliary lower bound to large permanent instances.
publisher_statement_or_check: In characteristic other than two, the flat hypothesis implies an eventual permanent lower bound exponential in (log₂ m)^(4/3).
review_finding: For each sufficiently large m, choose maximal r with 200r³≤⌊log₂m⌋. The projection fits at k=r² and ℓ=100r; its cost is at most 5s. The published /16 estimate suffices for log₂s>(log₂m)^(4/3)/1600².
independent_evidence_scope: 14A reconstructs integer bracketing, grid fit and affine gate overhead for HC (κ=40) and permanent (κ=3, 2≠0).
remaining_obligation: M.3 also requires the contracting-field rate, D.2 and transfer to a single comparison field for each characteristic.
review_detail: The transfer to HC and characteristic two proceeds via the separate grid-completeness route.

circuit_role: Convert contraction of matrix prices into geometric input for routing.
publisher_statement_or_check: A Poincaré inequality controls averages for the group action used by the contracting construction.
review_finding: The Poincaré constant is fixed before the dimension h. Telescoping the movement estimates avoids growth with the sliding-window count; the resulting uniform constant can fund G.2.
independent_evidence_scope: 13B traced the F.6 interface, window telescope, and caller. A fresh query reads F.6 in the full Paper.Laws closure.
remaining_obligation: Independently derive each F.2–F.5 angle, window and contraction estimate before invoking F.6.
review_detail: 12A traces downstream use of the Poincaré inequality and the norm constants. Proving it from the group/window estimates remains substantive.

circuit_role: Supply the algebraic laws that allow the contracting cut.
publisher_statement_or_check: The contracting hypothesis yields suitable laws over a finitely generated coefficient subring.
review_finding: A finite menu of rounded loads, a common tensor power and a label charged on every channel yield the required load norm. The gain constant is independent of h.
independent_evidence_scope: 13B derives the dual certificate, rounding and finite generation, tests both rounding directions, proves two scalar estimates in Lean and freshly rebuilds Paper.Laws.
remaining_obligation: 14B instantiates the G.2 laws in H.2; an independent full derivation of the earlier F.2–F.5 contraction mechanism is still a distinct human obligation.
review_detail: A small packet example cannot validate the existence of the laws for every required scale.

circuit_role: Supply a tower, cosets, and bounded-length routes to H.2.
publisher_statement_or_check: The tower has the size, incidence, action, and word-length properties needed for staged routing.
review_finding: Reduction of SL_h over the truncated binary ring has a trace-zero layer. A chain of 2-subgroups gives b-to-one chamber projections and bounded top size. Deleted-generator group actions are free and equivariant. A host bijection assigns exactly b children; layer lifting gives diameter O_h((n+1)^7). The printed cubic argument also follows from bounded wrapped-path seeds, balanced commutators, a shifted triangular basis and unit-pivot elimination.
independent_evidence_scope: 14B derived the subgroup, orbit, path and load claims; independently constructed a group of 43,008 elements and inspected 72,576 selected-edge routes with middle fibre eight and outer multiplicity at most two. The human cubic derivation gives length at most 4C_h(h−1)(h+9) times the sum of a² for a=1,…,n+1.
remaining_obligation: The independent h=3 finite check tests routing. The formal word diameter uses exponent seven. Certifying the stronger cubic estimate in Lean would be a distinct development.
review_detail: The cubic and seventh-power bounds both suffice for H.2. The bounded number of arbitrary-entry transvections uses the local binary ring and fixes h before n varies.

circuit_role: Turn an arbitrary weighted network into a bounded sum of outcomes without changing its scalar.
publisher_statement_or_check: For a valid initial load the network value equals a sum of endpoint contractions over bounded good outcomes.
review_finding: Relays insert equality tests. A connected law and a self-delimiting common sequence of indices give a full weighted identity after summing good outcomes and shared assignments. Terminal IDs, including t=0 cases, remain in the contraction when active.
independent_evidence_scope: 14B traces the concrete plan and checks all 16 boundary assignments in an independent signed two-layer law. Outcome contributions 3, −60 and 50 sum to −7. The integer norm bound floors 2C₁a₁² before multiplication by t².
remaining_obligation: The complete identity assumes valid G.2 tables and a commutative algebra over the coefficient ring; an individual outcome need not preserve the scalar.
review_detail: The good predicate is necessary for a possible outcome. It need not imply realizability. Dropping labels or the end packet gives 1 instead of 0 in the control.

circuit_role: Bound nonexceptional data incident to a piece and account separately for end packets.
publisher_statement_or_check: Every nonexceptional inter-node packet lies on a parent edge. At a single node the incident bound is Λ M^(1−γ)(N+M²); the global bound is Λ M(N+M²).
review_finding: For the least-energy type, Q′≤√(1+8C₁)Q/√h+dv′≤Q/2+dv′. Adjoining dv to Q absorbs rounding. Endpoint Cauchy–Schwarz, v_j=X/b^j and bounded top size give γ=1/log₂ b. The global charge sums over levels.
independent_evidence_scope: 14B reconstructs initial congestion 4m(N+X²), b middle preimages, two outer contributors and the local/global sums. A collapsed host choice gives 64 children when b=8.
remaining_obligation: This controls live loads. H.2(d,e) count consumed copies and program costs separately; J.2 additionally pays M^Cℓ for exceptional packet bits.
review_detail: The published gain admits the formal factor eight. Terminal IDs can join arbitrary nodes; they are charged in J.2 even at zero layers.

circuit_role: Provide a universal weighted evaluator for plain program inputs.
publisher_statement_or_check: The automaton produces the same total accepting weight within a quasi-linear simulation budget.
review_finding: The pointer encoding preserves each surviving trace's weight and multiplicity. Zero-weight branches can disappear; the final matrix stage preserves the scalar.
independent_evidence_scope: Pass 5 compared actual source semantics, checked finite traces in small rings and replayed focused Lean examples/arithmetic.
remaining_obligation: Independently derive sorting and address-width costs across all inputs. The complete package replay and Comparator belong to the two formal rows.
review_detail: An unqualified accepting-run bijection on p. 50 is too strong. The downstream J.3 and K.3 calls need the scalar and admitted time bound.

circuit_role: Express the automaton value as a tensor network that can be cut.
publisher_statement_or_check: Boundary states and packet counts expand the bounded automaton contraction.
review_finding: A count vector beyond the incident bound contributes zero through a local table factor, so it can be removed before the tree law.
independent_evidence_scope: Interface and zero-factor argument traced in 11C.
remaining_obligation: Reconstruct the full run-to-network equality and its bit/work accounting independently.
review_detail: Only after filtering valid counts do the H.2 and J.2 outcome and partition bounds apply.

circuit_role: Factor a bounded good outcome into smaller weighted pieces.
publisher_statement_or_check: One shared boundary value per current cut packet factors the weighted sum; each piece has controlled cut bits, total bits and size.
review_finding: Restriction and gluing are inverse assignments. A single boundary node charges all cut edges of a piece; copies, padding and given work require further charges.
independent_evidence_scope: 11C reconstructed gluing and boundary charging. 14B supplied the concrete tower plan, ever-held copy counts and a rederivation of the exceptional-bit charge.
remaining_obligation: The H.2 input and J.2 exceptional-bit charge are reconstructed in 14B. Independently audit the full pieces-program indexing and listing implementation at J.2–J.3.
review_detail: The network is the evaluator's transformed network. The source circuit is allowed arbitrary wiring. 12A verifies the scalar recurrence and the separate M^C·ℓ ≤ T/v^300 budget.

circuit_role: Turn the J.2 factorization into a one-cut program for the accelerator.
publisher_statement_or_check: The program's weighted value is the sum of products of its piece values with time and size controls.
review_finding: The evaluator may omit an empty active-cut packet because its summand has a zero local factor. The bounded outcome domain suffices.
independent_evidence_scope: Pass 6 source reconstruction and finite perturbation checks; pass 11C strengthened the J.2 input.
remaining_obligation: Independently reconstruct the actual listing/evaluation implementation and its runtime under the stated input bounds.
review_detail: The local packet checks support weighted-value equality, not equality of all guessed-run counts.

circuit_role: Preserve the value and resource bounds under repeated cuts.
publisher_statement_or_check: Iterated one-cut yields the cutting hypothesis on the permitted instances and scales.
review_finding: Parentheses, rounding, stopping and listing costs are charged as cuts compose. The caller supplies the cut hypothesis used by K.6.
independent_evidence_scope: 6 reconstructed iteration at its stated interfaces. 14E followed the resulting single setting into K.6.
remaining_obligation: 14B supplies H.2’s concrete input; 14E locates the one fixed cutting setting. Independently audit all machine-level recursive listings and their cumulative resource bounds.
review_detail: The number, time and maximum size of the pieces must hold together for the same original program instance.

circuit_role: Force an arbitrary small circuit into the contracting model.
publisher_statement_or_check: A circuit for the auxiliary polynomial yields a nondeterministic weighted evaluator for its low-degree part.
review_finding: A gate-indexed coefficient recurrence with ordered sockets yields a continuation invariant W(b,L). The potential 2b+|L| falls once per leaf/split. For d≥1 this bounds each path by 2d−1 rounds. Each occurrence of a billed coefficient name contributes a factor in its accepting run.
independent_evidence_scope: 14C reconstructs all short-input halting, the accepting-time bound, name height, program size and arbitrary shared gates. Across four rings 3,640 exact gate/code/cutoff comparisons include repeated operands, zero divisors and cancellation.
remaining_obligation: The theorem provides per-accepting-run step bounds and finite nonuniform advice. A deterministic sum-over-runs time bound or bit complexity for arbitrary ring constants is a different claim.
review_detail: This is a nonuniform weighted program with a per-accepting-run time bound. An ordinary deterministic Boolean evaluator would be a different claim.

circuit_role: Turn a hypothesized target circuit into an accelerator on plain instances.
publisher_statement_or_check: Circuit evaluation of an encoding polynomial reproduces the universal weighted value for bounded short words.
review_finding: Canonical marked-code agreement plus the degree bound gives the required value through K.2. I.1 fixes a common simulator; a ≤5s grid substitution and scale absorption meet every HasAcc resource field. The original source circuit still computes its target as a formal polynomial.
independent_evidence_scope: 14C derives the actual thresholds and obligations for all short inputs, distinguishes unconditional halting from equality on plain inputs, and checks the canonical-code/off-code distinction explicitly.
remaining_obligation: The printed word-sum polynomial and the concrete Lean extension can differ on malformed codes. The narrow canonical-code theorem suffices. K.6 still needs a separate diagonal and finite-field argument.
review_detail: The downstream interface requires the degree bound, promised evaluation and circuit transfer rather than equality of all internal path counts.

circuit_role: Allow repeated cuts to manipulate named constants within the plainness promise.
publisher_statement_or_check: The postponement transformation separates recording of named constants from the relevant program-evaluation phase.
review_finding: Its tally expansion postpones evaluation of named factors. At K.6 the exponents of the generated bills and the coefficients λ^e must agree on both sides of self-application.
independent_evidence_scope: 14E traces this interface through the finite-field specialization and diagonal value calculation. The transformation's full implementation has not been independently derived by hand.
remaining_obligation: Audit each accepting run, the timing and multiplicity of its output tally, and overhead for arbitrary programs.
review_detail: The identity concerns weights under the stated hypotheses. Uniform halting and the conditional value guarantee must remain distinct.

circuit_role: Propagate a hypothetical accelerator to the next scale.
publisher_statement_or_check: Cutting plus the previous accelerator yields a faster evaluator under a fixed system of size and exponent bounds.
review_finding: The number of pieces times work per piece and the separate listing cost fit the next budget once the scale condition absorbs fixed factors.
independent_evidence_scope: Passes 3 and 6 reconstructed the rate calculation at the stated interfaces.
remaining_obligation: Independently reconstruct the recursive program, including its listing, cut, scale and encoding costs. Pass 14E identifies its use before diagonalization.
review_detail: Arithmetic for one round needs the same instance to satisfy the J.4 listing, length and value promises.

circuit_role: Rule out the accelerator implied by a small circuit.
publisher_statement_or_check: With the cutting hypothesis and a finitely generated coefficient algebra, a diagonal program contradicts an accelerator at sufficiently large scales.
review_finding: Bounded-input halting and accepting time license K.4 postponement after checking bill length and the lookup for each name. The postponed instances have empty bills and fit the accepting-time budget. Their plainness licenses the value equality V=1+V in the nonzero finite field.
independent_evidence_scope: 14E traced the self-input contracts, coefficient agreement and order of quantifiers; 14C matched the excluded accelerator with K.3 at the same field and scale.
